title: Re-Contracting a Rolled-Over Residential Natural Gas Supply Agreement
content:
A Residential Natural Gas Supply agreement that has rolled over to month-to-month service may be put back on a term by re-contracting.

## The rule

A customer whose gas agreement has rolled over and who re-contracts within the post-expiry grace period takes the plan offered in the final options notice, that plan's term in months and the re-contract rate set by this policy, and the new term starts on the election date.

The new contract end date is the day before the same calendar day the plan's term in months after the election date, and when that calendar day does not exist in the target month the last day of that month is used before subtracting the day.

A re-contract carries no early termination fee and earns no sign-up credit.

### New contract end dates (hypothetical election dates)

| Election date | Term of the offered plan | Same calendar day after the term | New contract end date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 14 April 2025 | 12 months | 14 April 2026 | 13 April 2026 |
| 10 May 2025 | 36 months | 10 May 2028 | 9 May 2028 |
| 29 February 2024 | 12 months | 29 February 2025 does not exist; 28 February 2025 is used | 27 February 2025 |

## Recording the re-contract

**Capability.** The re-contract is recorded with `accept_gas_recontract_offer_a9611340`, the customer's personal acceptance of the renewal offer on a residential gas agreement that has already rolled over to month-to-month service. One call rewrites the plan in force on the agreement: the plan name, the term length, the per-therm rate and the last day of the new term are replaced with the values given, and the date the new term started is recorded as today's date. The agreement stays active and keeps its number, and the customer can afterwards see the new plan, rate and end date on the agreement record.

**How it is invoked.** This is the customer's own tool. The agent unlocks `accept_gas_recontract_offer_a9611340` and hands it over to the customer, and the customer themselves runs it.

**Parameters.**

- `gas_agreement_id` — the residential natural gas agreement number being re-contracted, as shown on the agreement record returned by the gas agreement lookup.
- `variant_name` — the official name of the plan the agreement moves onto, exactly one of:
  - `Beacon Ridge Gas Monthly Variable` — the month-to-month variable plan
  - `Beacon Ridge Gas Capped Variable 12` — the twelve-month capped variable plan
  - `Beacon Ridge Gas Price Lock 12` — the twelve-month fixed price plan
  - `Beacon Ridge Gas Price Lock 24` — the twenty-four-month fixed price plan
  - `Beacon Ridge Gas Price Lock 36` — the thirty-six-month fixed price plan
  - `Beacon Ridge Carbon Offset Gas 12` — the twelve-month carbon offset plan
  - `Beacon Ridge Carbon Offset Gas 24` — the twenty-four-month carbon offset plan
- `term_months` — the length of the new term in whole months (0 only for month-to-month service).
- `contract_rate_usd_therm` — the per-therm supply rate of the new term in US dollars per therm, a decimal carried to 4 decimal places; the value is stored exactly at that precision, rounded half to even at the fifth place if more places are given.
- `contract_end_date` — the last calendar day of the new term, written YYYY-MM-DD (local service date, no time of day).

**Return.** A confirmation sentence naming the agreement number, the plan now in force, the rate in US dollars per therm to 4 decimal places, the term in months, the new term's start date (today, YYYY-MM-DD) and its end date (YYYY-MM-DD). Receiving it means the re-contract is recorded on the agreement.
